bio.en: Hila Qu is a product-led growth expert best known for her two-part newsletter series on building a product-led growth motion—two of the most-read posts in Lenny's newsletter history—and for advising startups on activation, retention, and funnel optimization.
bio.zh: Hila Qu 是一位产品驱动增长（PLG）专家，她关于如何搭建 PLG 增长体系的两篇系列文章，是 Lenny newsletter 历史上阅读量最高的文章之二；她还就用户激活、留存与漏斗优化为众多初创公司提供顾问指导。

summary.en: Hila breaks down how to start and optimize a product-led growth motion, beginning with the foundational idea of data-led growth: give away a free product, but in return capture broader reach and, crucially, usage data that reveals which features predict conversion and retention. She walks through the common pitfalls teams hit when getting started, her recommended tools for an initial PLG-oriented team, and how to audit an existing funnel for leaks. The conversation also goes deep on improving activation and retention, plus a clear overview of core PLG concepts like balancing free reach with analytical rigor. Listeners come away with a concrete, high-value playbook for standing up PLG the right way.
summary.zh: Hila 拆解了如何启动并优化产品驱动增长体系，起点是“数据驱动增长”这一基础理念：把免费产品送出去，但作为交换，要获得更广泛的触达，更重要的是拿到使用数据，从而看清哪些功能预示着转化和留存。她梳理了团队刚起步时最常踩的坑、为初始 PLG 团队推荐的工具，以及如何审计现有漏斗找出漏点。对话还深入探讨了如何提升激活和留存，并清晰讲解了 PLG 的核心概念，比如在免费触达和分析严谨之间取得平衡。听众最终会收获一份具体、高价值、能真正落地搭建 PLG 的实战手册。

turns.zh: 好的，完美。我认为这真的很有帮助。我认为我们深入探讨了我们计划的讨论的一些核心内容，我认为从人们在尝试添加产品主导的增长动议时陷入的常见陷阱开始会很有趣。那么，当人们试图找出产品主导型增长时，最常见的失败方式是什么？

turns.speaker: Hila Qu
turns.en: The first of all, as I mentioned, you need to have some sort of vehicle. A lot of the companies, if you go to their website, especially B2B companies, you'll see the biggest CTA is called book demo. They don't have anything else. The first step for you to do is submit a form and kind of basically explain yourself to this company, I'm from who and who company and I want to use the tool, can you come back to me and allow me to see a demo of your product? That means the entry point to PLG is cut off. Instead, the first step is you need to either have a free product, free trial, some sort of a low barrier entry for anyone who stumble upon this product to give it a try. A lot of companies don't have that. That's the first I would say hurdle or peaceful. (00:12:38): And especially if you are a sales lead and you already have all those things figured out, you try to go to add PLG, it's not as easy as just say, add a kind of free trial CTA on your website. You need to build this free experience. You also need to convince your sales team, your existing product team, your marketing team, "Hey, let's try this out." Because before this process is super clean. Everyone only get only selected future leads and sales work on those. But now you need to allow more people in and there need to be more understanding of their behavior data, the process need to change. So it's actually a whole process. So I would say that's first one. And along with that is some companies didn't think it thoroughly and they are just kind of saying, "Oh, PLG is cool, let's do PLG." (00:13:34): And then they maybe spend three months build kind of some sort of a very basic free trial and then they think that's it. They think the leads will come, conversion will come, self-service revenue will come. It's not that easy. It's not that simple. It is definitely a entire motion. So I would say you need to commit to it. Maybe you can do some thinking, collecting some data, build your conviction, but to a certain point you need to commit to at least a year or even two years kind of roadmap to build this entire thing out and change the process internally sometimes as well to support that. The last one, I would say a lot of times the company's committed, they want to do this, but they don't know the right way or they don't have the foundation, they don't have the expertise of PLG. (00:14:27): Their internal team, they're really good at sales or maybe really good at as the traditional motion, but they don't have this part of expertise and foundation. A common thing I see is that company want to do PLG and they have no usage data at all and they're like, "I will just doing PLG. But PLG I always say is actually fundamentally DLG, data led growth. So when you give away your free product, what you want to get in exchange are two things. One is the broader reach because free product spread itself is lower barrier to entry. Two, you want to understand the usage behavior of those free users, which features do they use and which features kind of correlates with a higher conversion rate, retention rate, all of that. (00:15:20): If you don't have a foundation of data and understanding of how to analyze those data, you are giving a way of free product for nothing. Like you are really not being able to utilize all of that to build your PLG motion. So I think data foundation and expertise in terms of how do I design that user journey, that journey is very different from the sales user journey. Those are sometimes missing in company when they just begin to doing this. And in those cases I think it's super helpful to maybe either find someone who have done this as an advisor or hire someone like you need to have that expertise or through advisor to support your PLG motion.
turns.zh: 首先，正如我提到的，你需要拥有某种车辆。很多公司，如果你去他们的网站，特别是B2B公司，你会看到最大的CTA叫做图书演示。他们没有别的东西了。您要做的第一步是提交一份表格，并向这家公司基本解释一下自己，我来自谁、谁公司，我想使用该工具，您能回到我身边，让我看看您产品的演示吗？这意味着 PLG 的入口点被切断。相反，第一步是您需要获得免费产品、免费试用，或者为任何偶然发现该产品的人提供某种低门槛的入口来尝试。很多公司都没有这个。这是我首先要说的障碍或和平。 (00:12:38)：特别是如果您是销售主管，并且您已经解决了所有这些问题，那么您尝试去添加 PLG，这并不像在您的网站上添加一种免费试用 CTA 那样简单。您需要构建这种免费体验。您还需要说服您的销售团队、现有的产品团队、营销团队，“嘿，让我们尝试一下。”因为之前这个过程是超级干净的。每个人只能获得选定的未来线索，并针对这些线索进行销售工作。但现在你需要让更多的人进来，需要更多地了解他们的行为数据，这个过程需要改变。所以这实际上是一个完整的过程。所以我想说这是第一个。除此之外，一些公司没有彻底思考这一点，他们只是说，“哦，PLG 很酷，我们就做 PLG 吧。” (00:13:34)：然后他们可能会花三个月的时间构建某种非常基本的免费试用版，然后他们认为就这样了。他们认为潜在客户将会到来，转化将会到来，自助服务收入将会到来。这并不容易。事情没那么简单。这绝对是一个完整的运动。所以我想说你需要承诺这一点。也许你可以做一些思考，收集一些数据，建立你的信念，但到了一定程度，你需要承诺至少一年甚至两年的路线图来构建整个事情，有时也需要在内部改变流程来支持这一点。最后一个，我想说很多时候公司承诺，他们想要这样做，但他们不知道正确的方法，或者他们没有基础，他们没有PLG的专业知识。 (00:14:27): 他们的内部团队，他们真的很擅长销售或者可能真的很擅长传统的动作，但是他们没有这部分的专业知识和基础。我看到的一个常见现象是，公司想要做 PLG，但他们根本没有使用数据，他们会说，“我只会做 PLG。但我总是说 PLG 实际上从根本上来说是 DLG，数据主导增长。因此，当你赠送免费产品时，你想要交换的是两件事。一是更广泛的覆盖面，因为免费产品传播本身降低了进入门槛。二是你想了解这些免费用户的使用行为，他们使用哪些功能以及哪些功能与某个功能相关。更高的转化率、留存率等等（00:15:20）：如果您没有数据基础并且不了解如何分析这些数据，那么您实际上无法利用所有这些来构建您的 PLG 动议，因此我认为，在公司刚开始这样做时，这些数据基础和专业知识与销售用户旅程非常不同。我认为，找到做过这件事的人作为顾问，或者聘请像您需要具备专业知识的人，或者通过顾问来支持您的 PLG 动议，这是非常有帮助的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: This is great. We're going to talk about the data piece more in depth later, but on the commitment piece, I thought that was really interesting. I imagine many times founders or leaders think they have commitment and then they realize maybe not so much. Are there any kind of flags that tell you that, "Oh, you're not actually committed to working on this for a year or two years, whatever it takes."
turns.zh: 这太棒了。稍后我们将更深入地讨论数据部分，但关于承诺部分，我认为这非常有趣。我想很多时候，创始人或领导者认为他们有承诺，然后他们意识到可能没有那么多。是否有任何类型的标志告诉您，“哦，您实际上并没有致力于为此工作一年或两年，无论付出什么代价。”

turns.speaker: Hila Qu
turns.en: The red flags I've seen basically sometimes, first of all, they think about PLG equals launch of free version or launch of free trial. They made this assumption in their head, "Oh, I already have a product. I already have a software that's working, customers are using. Now if I add a free version, if I open a free trial, that's it." Like that's basically PLG, and I will have conversions. I will have people becoming a product qualified leads just because I have it. "Hey, I open this for you, just come and use it and [inaudible 00:17:07]." And I think that's one red flag. Basically they are not thinking about the entire thing through understanding the implication, not only the free product, it's really just a start. You need to think about how to activate, how to design the upgrade path, how those teams, those new growth teams work with other sales and marketing teams, all of that. (00:17:29): So that's one. The other one is they don't have a dedicated team. They just basically assign one person to the thing. They are imagine, "Hey, you already have this. It's not that big of deal. You can just figure this out by borrowing resources from everywhere and try to coordinate all the stakeholders from sales, marketing, product." That person need to be a magician in order to be successful in that basically. And I think the third thing is basically they are really doing this because it's trendy. They didn't think about the deeper strategic reason why this is a good fit for their business. Do you have a product that's relatively low complexity, doesn't require a lot of customization for the customer to see value. (00:18:19): Time to value need to be relatively short or you can figure out a way to make it short. And then do you have a lot of potentially end user S&B business? They are interested in the solution. They want to try that out. If you do not have both, if you for example, develop a software for the [inaudible 00:18:42]. Companies like [inaudible 00:18:44]. Or defense companies, only three target customer exist in the entire world, you don't probably want to do PLG, right? So think deeper about the fit and then commit. And I would say those are the red flags.
turns.zh: 我有时看到的危险信号基本上是，首先，他们认为 PLG 等于推出免费版本或推出免费试用版。他们在脑海中做出了这样的假设：“哦，我已经有了一个产品。我已经有了一个可以运行的软件，客户正在使用。现在，如果我添加一个免费版本，如果我打开一个免费试用版，就这样了。”就像这基本上是 PLG，我会进行转换。我会让人们成为产品合格的领导者，因为我拥有它。 “嘿，我为你打开这个，只需过来使用它即可 [听不清 00:17:07]。”我认为这是一个危险信号。基本上他们并没有通过理解含义来思考整个事情，不仅仅是免费产品，这实际上只是一个开始。你需要考虑如何激活，如何设计升级路径，这些团队，那些新的增长团队如何与其他销售和营销团队合作，所有这些。 (00:17:29)：就是这样。另一个是他们没有专门的团队。他们基本上只是指派一个人来做这件事。他们想象，“嘿，你已经有了这个。这没什么大不了的。你可以通过借用各地的资源来解决这个问题，并尝试协调来自销售、营销、产品的所有利益相关者。”这个人必须是一名魔术师才能在这方面取得成功。我认为第三件事基本上是他们真的这样做是因为它很流行。他们没有考虑为什么这非常适合他们的业务的更深层次的战略原因。您是否拥有复杂性相对较低、不需要大量定制即可让客户看到价值的产品？ (00:18:19)：实现价值的时间需要相对较短，或者您可以找到一种方法来缩短它。那么您是否有很多潜在的最终用户 S&B 业务？他们对解决方案感兴趣。他们想尝试一下。如果您两者都没有，例如，如果您为 [听不清 00:18:42] 开发一个软件。像 [听不清 00:18:44] 这样的公司。或者国防公司，全世界只有三个目标客户，你可能不想做PLG，对吧？因此，请更深入地考虑是否适合，然后做出承诺。我想说这些都是危险信号。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay. So on that last point, I thought that was a really interesting, we talked about how every company probably should add a product led growth piece, but I think what you're also saying is actually not every company, there are some companies like defense contractors that are probably going to be sale led.
turns.zh: 好的。因此，关于最后一点，我认为这非常有趣，我们讨论了每个公司可能应该如何添加产品主导的增长部分，但我认为您所说的实际上并不是每个公司，有些公司（例如国防承包商）可能会以销售为主导。

turns.speaker: Hila Qu
turns.en: I think it's a spectrum. I would say the defense company, defense software company is a pretty extreme example. And of course in those case, I don't think it makes sense, but I think majority of B2B software, I've seen, you've seen, we've used even some more complicated ones. Like Salesforce used to be this example of sales motion. They're the pioneer of SaaS and they do this so well, but they begin to add look into sales service portal and all of that. And even a lot of the bigger players are looking into that. So I think majority of the B2B software, probably they are in the middle of the spectrum rather than the defense company.
turns.zh: 我认为这是一个频谱。我想说国防公司、国防软件公司是一个非常极端的例子。当然，在这种情况下，我认为这是没有意义的，但我认为大多数 B2B 软件，我见过，你也见过，我们甚至使用了一些更复杂的软件。就像 Salesforce 曾经是这个销售动议的例子一样。他们是 SaaS 的先驱，他们在这方面做得非常好，但他们开始添加对销售服务门户等的关注。甚至许多较大的参与者也在研究这个问题。所以我认为大多数 B2B 软件可能处于中间范围，而不是国防公司。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: You kind of shared some of the attributes of what allows you to be product led, like quick time to value. If you have this in your head, what are some of those bullet points of what you need to figure out for it to be successful potentially as product led?
turns.zh: 您分享了一些让您能够以产品为主导的属性，例如快速实现价值。如果你脑子里有这个想法，那么你需要弄清楚哪些要点才能以产品为主导，从而取得潜在的成功？

turns.speaker: Hila Qu
turns.en: The first thing is that have a... And you mentioned you are able to have a vehicle, have a free version, have a free trial. Sometimes it's a open source product. A lot of developer products start as a open source product. It has its constraints, but it is also a great kind of vehicle for PLG or if none of those are option, you can build a really realistic kind of experience. For example, I remember Amplitude, they are pursuing PLG now, but they used to have a lot of barrier. As an end user, it's hard for me to put that code into my product and see my data, but they build a really realistic interactive demo that's getting closer to PLG. So it's not PLG, but it's getting closer and you can already see the value and play with it yourself. So that's the first step. Have a vehicle. (00:21:18): The second step step is time to value. Basically, just because you have this vehicle doesn't mean people will come and use it and see the value. So you need to figure out how do you give your users a warm start and help them get started. I was talking with a kind of company today, they just realized we have this tool and when people come in into the free trial, they are asked to do some action, but nobody know how to do that. They may not have everything ready to take that action. So we're like, "What about we gave them some sample video or sample action they can try." Right? It's not the same as they do it themselves, but it's better. It's getting closer. And after that you can ask them to try the thing on their own and they need to do more work. (00:22:07): So kind of think about all the ways you can reduce time to value. It doesn't need to be this big aha moment in the first five minutes, but at least give them some mini aha moments, right? So that's the second thing, third thing is think about from there. If they get aha moment, if they want to buy, you need to have this self-checkout flow ready, self-service flow. It's the foundation, if you have it, it doesn't mean they won't buy immediately, but at least it gave them this option to do that themselves. And the fourth thing I would say, between this kind of activation usage, aha moment to this conversion moment, actually there's a big gap. And what is the gap? How you can understand the gap, how you can guide people around that journey is basically you need to have a very good grasp of data. (00:23:03): You need to have the foundation to understand their usage, their behavior, and then you can design a user journey in the product, in email, in all those tools to guide user to the next step. So have a very strong data foundation there. I would say. I think those are the main thing. And there are other things like your pricing need to be relatively simple. If your pricing is super complicated, they need to... Whenever they pick, for example, they try the product, they love it, they have a self-checkout flow, but in order to decide how much they need to pay, they need to send your sales some information, you need to do a quote, then that's broken, right? Or they're already confused about this process. So that is another kind of important thing as well.
turns.zh: 首先，你提到你可以拥有一辆车，有一个免费版本，有一个免费试用版。有时它是开源产品。许多开发人员产品都是从开源产品开始的。它有其局限性，但它也是 PLG 的一种很好的工具，或者如果这些都不是选项，您可以构建一种真正现实的体验。比如我记得Amplitude，他们现在在追求PLG，但是他们以前有很多障碍。作为最终用户，我很难将该代码放入我的产品中并查看我的数据，但他们构建了一个非常现实的交互式演示，越来越接近 PLG。所以它不是 PLG，但它越来越接近，你已经可以看到它的价值并自己使用它。这是第一步。有车。 (00:21:18)：第二步是实现价值的时间。基本上，仅仅因为你拥有这辆车并不意味着人们会来使用它并看到它的价值。因此，您需要弄清楚如何为用户提供一个温暖的开始并帮助他们开始使用。我今天与一家公司交谈，他们刚刚意识到我们有这个工具，当人们进入免费试用版时，他们被要求做一些操作，但没有人知道如何做。他们可能还没有做好采取这一行动的一切准备。所以我们想，“我们给他们一些可以尝试的示例视频或示例动作怎么样？”正确的？这和他们自己做的不一样，但是更好。越来越近了。之后你可以要求他们自己尝试，他们需要做更多的工作。 (00:22:07)：请考虑一下可以缩短价值实现时间的所有方法。前五分钟不需要有这么大的顿悟时刻，但至少给他们一些迷你的顿悟时刻，对吧？这是第二件事，第三件事是从那里开始思考。如果他们顿悟了，如果他们想购买，你需要准备好自助结帐流程，自助服务流程。这是基础，如果你有了它，并不意味着他们不会立即购买，但至少它给了他们自己这样做的选择。第四点我要说的是，这种激活使用、顿悟时刻和转换时刻之间，实际上有很大的差距。差距是多少？如何理解差距，如何引导人们完成这一旅程基本上是你需要很好地掌握数据。 (00:23:03)：您需要具备了解他们的使用情况、行为的基础，然后您可以在产品、电子邮件和所有这些工具中设计用户旅程，以引导用户进行下一步。因此，那里有非常强大的数据基础。我会说。我认为这些是主要的事情。还有其他一些事情，比如你的定价需要相对简单。如果你的定价非常复杂，他们需要......每当他们挑选时，例如，他们尝试产品，他们喜欢它，他们有自助结账流程，但为了决定他们需要支付多少钱，他们需要向你的销售人员发送一些信息，你需要做一个报价，那么这就坏了，对吧？或者他们已经对这个过程感到困惑了。所以这也是另一件重要的事情。

turns.en: Awesome. Okay, so we've been going in a lot of directions. We started with pitfalls and things you probably will... You'll run into that may set you off track. But let's zoom out again and let's get into, just say you're convinced we need to invest in adding a product-led growth motion to our product. What's the first step that you recommend for people to go down?
turns.zh: 惊人的。好的，我们已经朝很多方向前进了。我们从陷阱和你可能会遇到的事情开始......你会遇到这些可能会让你偏离正轨的事情。但是，让我们再次缩小范围，让我们进入，只是说您确信我们需要投资为我们的产品添加以产品为主导的增长动力。您建议人们向下走的第一步是什么？

turns.speaker: Hila Qu
turns.en: I think the first step actually, I would recommend founders and leaders to just understand what's PLG funnel, what's sales-led funnel with SLG funnel. Because I remember when I begin to work on PLG at GitLab, it was not that clear to me. There's a lot of things you can read, but they're not all super clear. What is PLG? How is that different? And through working on that myself, I begin to develop this conviction and kind of this clear picture. The biggest difference from SLG and PLG is that the sales funnel traditionally work like something... You have marketing team working on the top of funnel, bring visitor and then they need to have a process to turn the visitors into lead. And leads is something, it is basically very popular and vitally used in the B2B business. And you go through some qualification process and leads need to be from your target kind of customer, target industry. (00:26:23): The company need to meet certain size, but they also need to show interest. And how marketing team historically gauge interest is how much they interact with your marketing campaigns. Do they open an email? Do they read three white papers? Do they go to this webinar? That's how they gauge interest. And for each positive action you did as a buyer, they add some points to you. And once you reach certain points, you become this marketing qualified leads. Basically those are the better ones we featured through that process and we gave that to the sales team. And sales team has more process, but then they choose some of them, work on them, and they close some of them. So that's kind of traditionally B2B sales-led motion works. And then product-led funnel is different. It's much more similar to B2C. Basically you can still have people visit your website and they sign up for free version or free account or free trial. (00:27:21): The most important thing, the biggest difference, is now you want them to use the product. You can still send all the marketing emails, all of that, but those are supplemental. Those are kind of trying to get them to the product to use, to try, and the usage, product usage, is almost like the leading indicator for success for PLG, versus in the sales funnel, it's almost like how many do you get and do they interact with the marketing campaigns, which in the old days it's what you have because nobody can access your product unless the contract is signed. But nowadays that's almost like an artificial barrier. It's not there. You can totally build a product in a free version to allow people to use. So usage becomes so important. And that's the biggest difference from the usage that you have two potential conversion paths. (00:28:18): One is that if this product is not that expensive, the price point fits in most companies' budget. Some companies may just use their credit card and they buy online. That's also, you then don't even need sales team to be involved. And it's very similar to the B2C product, e-commerce product, buying process. And it's awesome because it's automated, you don't need to have more sales team involved. It's low cost, it's efficient, it can happen on its own every day. It will just add up to your revenue. And then the other potential conversion pass is where the product usage is high, but also this customer, this potential prospect, fits into your ideal customer profile. It's from a Fortune 500 company or it's from a target industry that you know they need your solution. Then this customer worth more of your time and you should actually not, even if they may want to buy on their own, you may want to still have your sales team or have your customer success team to reach out to them to understand a little bit more of the situation and give them some white glove service. Hopefully you can even close a bigger deal than if they would have buy on their own. So that's another pass. I call that PQL, PQA, like sales pass.
turns.zh: 我认为实际上第一步，我会建议创始人和领导者了解什么是 PLG 漏斗，什么是销售主导漏斗和 SLG 漏斗。因为我记得当我开始在 GitLab 从事 PLG 工作时，我并不太清楚。您可以阅读很多内容，但它们并不都非常清晰。什么是PLG？那有什么不同呢？通过我自己的努力，我开始形成这种信念和清晰的图景。与 SLG 和 PLG 最大的区别在于，销售漏斗传统上的工作方式类似于...营销团队在漏斗顶部工作，带来访客，然后他们需要有一个流程将访客转化为潜在客户。潜在客户是一种东西，它基本上非常流行，并且在 B2B 业务中得到广泛使用。你要经历一些资格认证过程，并且线索需要来自你的目标客户类型、目标行业。 (00:26:23)：公司需要达到一定的规模，但他们也需要表现出兴趣。营销团队历来衡量兴趣的方式是他们与您的营销活动互动的程度。他们会打开电子邮件吗？他们读过三份白皮书吗？他们参加这个网络研讨会吗？这就是他们衡量兴趣的方式。对于您作为买家所做的每一项积极行动，他们都会为您增加一些积分。一旦你达到了一定的程度，你就成为了营销合格的领导者。基本上，这些是我们通过该过程推荐的更好的产品，并将其提供给销售团队。销售团队有更多的流程，但他们会选择其中的一些，对其进行处理，然后关闭其中的一些。这就是传统上 B2B 销售主导的运动作品。然后以产品为主导的漏斗是不同的。它与 B2C 更相似。基本上，您仍然可以让人们访问您的网站，并注册免费版本或免费帐户或免费试用版。 (00:27:21)：最重要的、最大的区别是现在你希望他们使用该产品。您仍然可以发送所有营销电子邮件，所有这些，但这些都是补充性的。这些都是试图让他们使用、尝试产品，而使用情况、产品使用情况几乎就像是 PLG 成功的主要指标，而在销售漏斗中，这几乎就像你得到了多少产品以及他们是否与营销活动互动，这在过去就是你所拥有的，因为除非签署合同，否则没有人可以访问你的产品。但如今这几乎就像一个人为的屏障。它不在那里。您完全可以构建免费版本的产品以供人们使用。所以使用就变得如此重要。这与使用情况最大的区别是有两个潜在的转化路径。 (00:28:18)：一是如果这个产品不是那么贵，那么价格点就适合大多数公司的预算。有些公司可能只使用信用卡并在网上购买。也就是说，您甚至不需要销售团队参与。这与B2C产品、电子商务产品的购买流程非常相似。它很棒，因为它是自动化的，您不需要更多的销售团队参与。它成本低，效率高，每天都可以发生。它只会增加您的收入。然后另一个潜在的转化通道是产品使用率很高的地方，而且这个客户，这个潜在的潜在客户，也符合你理想的客户档案。它来自财富 500 强公司或者来自您知道他们需要您的解决方案的目标行业。那么这个客户值得你花更多的时间，而你实际上不应该，即使他们可能想自己购买，你可能仍然希望你的销售团队或你的客户成功团队与他们接触，以了解更多的情况，并为他们提供一些白手套服务。希望您甚至可以达成比他们自己购买更大的交易。所以这是另一次通过。我称之为 PQL、PQA，就像销售通行证一样。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And that stands for product qualified lead, right?
turns.zh: 这代表产品合格的铅，对吧？

turns.speaker: Hila Qu
turns.en: Product qualified leads, product qualified account. So the first step is for you to understand those two funnels and then think about if you want to add PLG, right? What is this journey? What are the steps along that funnel you need to establish for your product in order for your user to be able to convert in that funnel?
turns.zh: 产品合格的线索，产品合格的帐户。所以第一步是让你了解这两个渠道，然后考虑是否要添加 PLG，对吗？这次旅程是什么？为了让您的用户能够在该渠道中进行转化，您需要为您的产品建立哪些渠道步骤？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: So you talked about these two funnels. One question is, are they basically the same for almost every product or should you try to figure out what's really unique about my funnel? And then second, is there an example of product that you think about like, here's the sales led funnel for them and then here's the product-led version of that, just to make it a little more real even?
turns.zh: 所以你谈到了这两个渠道。一个问题是，几乎所有产品的它们基本上都是相同的，还是您应该尝试找出我的漏斗的真正独特之处？其次，您是否有一个产品示例，例如，这是他们的销售主导漏斗，然后是产品主导的版本，只是为了使其更加真实？

turns.speaker: Hila Qu
turns.en: Maybe I can give an example first and then we can talk about the other question. So I can use GitLab as an example since that's where I'm most familiar. GitLab actually have a enterprise sales team, very strong sales team, from the very beginning. But the company also we started from open source product.
turns.zh: 也许我可以先举个例子，然后我们再讨论另一个问题。所以我可以使用 GitLab 作为例子，因为那是我最熟悉的地方。 GitLab 实际上从一开始就拥有一支企业销售团队，非常强大的销售团队。但我们公司也是从开源产品开始的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Maybe describe what GitLab is for folks that aren't super familiar with it.
turns.zh: 也许可以为不太熟悉 GitLab 的人描述一下它是什么。

turns.speaker: Hila Qu
turns.en: Yeah, so GitLab, we are a developer platform, DevOps platform, basically engineer teams, developer teams. They use this product to manage their entire DevOps process, from storing their code, kind of managing the version control, releasing CSAD, like security scan, all of that. It's an all in one platform for that team. So for the sales-led motion, like I mentioned, the teams, our marketing team, were working bringing a lot of visitors to our website and they sign up for free trial, for free accounts. And then we have this lead nurturing and lead scoring process to surface which are the good ones for our sales team. In our sales team, we have SNB, we have the mid-market, we have enterprise, and they each kind of took their buckets of leads and work on them and close them. They become revenue. (00:31:52): And then how the product led funnel work for us is someone, maybe as a developer, I heard about GitLab, I go to website, I see, "Oh, I can actually sign up for a free account." I may use it for my personal project. My company may be using another solution, but I have some side project I'm doing as a developer. I want to use GitLab to host that. And I did that. And so you begin to see this, individual users having some usage but nothing to do with his company. And then one day maybe this person's employer, "We want to look into some other solutions. We have way too many point solutions for each step of DevOps. Now we want to potentially consolidate them. So what are the options?" And this engineer raise his hand, "Hey, I have been using GitLab for a very long time and I really like it. I think we should check them out." And then this team, maybe this engineer manager or CTO depending on the size of company, they're like, "Okay." (00:32:55): He went to their website and he kind of signed up for a free trial because that allow him to test some more advanced features. It's 30 days, but he already has... This person knows how to use it. This person already set up the foundation with the free version and they started the free trial. They use their 30 day to do a proof of concept, the entire company already using it for part of their process. And they're like, "Oh, awesome. I tried this feature, that feature, that feature. It's a great tool. It can support our workflow and I'm pretty sure we should be able to get ROI from this product." And then in this case they are like, "I only need five seats. It's cheap. I will just go to the pricing page and check out the pricing and buy from there." Or in some cases, this is a big company and we see this big company is using our product, our sales team get that data signal, they may send an email and reach out and say, "Hey, I saw you were checking it out. How can I help?" And that may start a sales conversation, eventually become a contract from there.
turns.zh: 是的，GitLab，我们是一个开发者平台，DevOps 平台，基本上是工程师团队，开发者团队。他们使用这个产品来管理整个 DevOps 流程，从存储代码、管理版本控制、发布 CSAD，如安全扫描，所有这些。对于该团队来说，这是一个一体化平台。因此，对于以销售为主导的动议，就像我提到的那样，我们的团队、我们的营销团队正在努力吸引大量访问者访问我们的网站，他们注册免费试用、免费帐户。然后我们就有了潜在客户培育和潜在客户评分流程，这对我们的销售团队来说是好事。在我们的销售团队中，我们有 SNB，我们有中端市场，我们有企业，他们各自抓住了大量的潜在客户，并致力于它们并关闭它们。它们变成了收入。 (00:31:52)：然后产品引导漏斗如何为我们工作的是某人，也许作为开发人员，我听说过 GitLab，我访问网站，我看到，“哦，我实际上可以注册一个免费帐户。”我可以将它用于我的个人项目。我的公司可能正在使用另一种解决方案，但我作为开发人员正在做一些副业项目。我想使用 GitLab 来托管它。我就这么做了。所以你开始看到这一点，个人用户有一些使用，但与他的公司无关。然后有一天，也许这个人的雇主，“我们想研究一些其他解决方案。对于 DevOps 的每个步骤，我们都有太多的单点解决方案。现在我们想要潜在地整合它们。那么有什么选择呢？”这位工程师举起了手，“嘿，我已经使用 GitLab 很长时间了，我真的很喜欢它。我想我们应该检查一下。”然后这个团队，也许是这个工程师经理或首席技术官，具体取决于公司的规模，他们会说，“好吧。” (00:32:55)：他访问了他们的网站，并注册了免费试用版，因为这使他能够测试一些更高级的功能。三十天了，但他已经……这个人知道怎么用了。此人已经通过免费版本建立了基础，并开始免费试用。他们用 30 天的时间进行概念验证，整个公司已经将其用于其流程的一部分。他们就像，“哦，太棒了。我尝试了这个功能，那个功能，那个功能。这是一个很棒的工具。它可以支持我们的工作流程，我很确定我们应该能够从这个产品中获得投资回报。”然后在这种情况下，他们会说，“我只需要五个座位。很便宜。我只需进入定价页面，查看定价并从那里购买。”或者在某些情况下，这是一家大公司，我们看到这家大公司正在使用我们的产品，我们的销售团队收到该数据信号，他们可能会发送一封电子邮件并伸出援手说：“嘿，我看到你正在检查它。我可以帮忙吗？”这可能会开始销售对话，最终成为合同。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Great. Thank you for sharing that example. Maybe a last question on this first step of mapping out the funnel. Do you recommend people just get in front of a whiteboard and just sit together and like, "Here's what it would be potentially if we added a product-led growth motion?"
turns.zh: 伟大的。感谢您分享该示例。也许是关于绘制漏斗的第一步的最后一个问题。你是否建议人们坐在白板前，坐在一起，说：“如果我们添加以产品为主导的增长动议，可能会出现什么结果？”

turns.speaker: Hila Qu
turns.en: Yes. Yes. And I think it's not that... The devil is in the details. Just mapping out the big steps is not that hard. You think about, " I have a marketing site already. I can build a free version." And then they use the free version and I build a checkout flow and that's it. That's the story. But that's the first step. If you don't even have those components, mapping out the funnel will allow you to see a missing checkout flow, a missing free version, you already identified that. But the devil is in the detail one layer down. How do you design an experience for each of the step? What do you say on your marketing side to drive free signup? In the free signup, how do you guide them to use the three most important features? And in the checkout flow, which payment option do you offer so that customers from everywhere can buy very smoothly? So that's the next layers kind of detail that actually has so many opportunities for optimization, maximization and all of that.
turns.zh: 是的。是的。我认为并非如此……细节决定成败。制定大步骤并不难。您会想，“我已经有了一个营销网站。我可以构建一个免费版本。”然后他们使用免费版本，我构建了一个结帐流程，仅此而已。这就是故事。但这是第一步。如果您甚至没有这些组件，绘制出漏斗图将使您能够看到缺少的结帐流程，缺少的免费版本，您已经确定了这一点。但问题在于下一层的细节。您如何为每个步骤设计体验？您认为营销方面如何推动免费注册？在免费注册中，你如何引导他们使用最重要的三个功能？那么在结账流程中，你们提供哪种支付方式让各地的顾客都可以非常顺利地购买呢？这就是下一层的细节，实际上有很多优化、最大化等机会。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That's actually a really good segue to the next question, which is just, okay, you've mapped out the funnel, what do you do next?
turns.zh: 这实际上是下一个问题的一个很好的延续，好吧，你已经绘制了漏斗图，接下来你要做什么？

turns.speaker: Hila Qu
turns.en: If you don't have the foundational components, you need to build all of that. But if you have something, if you already have this funnel exist, right, it's just not working perfectly at least, but it's working, it's there. I think the next step is you need to pick a starting point. Where do you want to focus first to drive the maximum impact? Personally, I'm a big fan of finding leverage. I think doing growth is always about finding leverage. If you can always find the area that with relatively small investment can give you the biggest results, that can be such a kind of momentum, can empower you through future experiments and more work. And just finding leverage is a beautiful thing in my mind. So I always want to do that. So when I think about pick a starting point, one thing I actually do with a lot of my advisory clients as a first step is, we do a full funnel audit, full PLG funnel audit. (00:36:38): Think about, we go through me as a kind of end user, go through the entire journey, pretend I am interested, semi interested, and I want to buy from the website. Does that kind of attract me? Is it super clear the value proposition? And then from there, going through the sign up of the free account or free trial, is that smooth? And when I begin to use the product, do I get to my aha moment fast or I am very confused and frustrated, abandoned at that moment? And from there, if I'm like, think this is good, right, I hit my aha moment, I want to buy. Can I even buy? You will never believe, like when I do this audit,, there are so many low hanging fruits usually in this process. For example, one client, when I go to the checkout flow, the kind of checkout form is so confusing. (00:37:38): They ask a bunch of questions that only let's say UK customer need. Every other places they don't need to answer, but they ask the question anyway. And I as a US based person is very confused and I drop off at that point. And then there are other things, for example, the aha moments like I talk about. I don't know what to do when I land inside a product for the first time, I'm super excited and ready, but I don't know what to do. I'm so lost and confused. That's usually a pretty big focus area and opportunity area. Just getting your users to aha moments. They are already over so many hurdles here, but don't just turn down them and they leave because it's so confusing.
turns.zh: 如果您没有基础组件，则需要构建所有这些组件。但如果你有一些东西，如果你已经有了这个漏斗，对吧，它至少不能完美地工作，但它正在工作，它就在那里。我认为下一步你需要选择一个起点。您想首先关注哪里以产生最大影响？就我个人而言，我非常热衷于寻找杠杆。我认为实现增长总是要找到杠杆。如果你总能找到用相对较小的投入就能给你带来最大成果的领域，那就可以是这样一种动力，可以让你通过未来的实验和更多的工作。在我看来，找到杠杆就是一件美好的事情。所以我一直想这样做。因此，当我考虑选择一个起点时，我实际上与许多咨询客户一起做的第一步是，我们进行完整的漏斗审计，完整的 PLG 漏斗审计。 (00:36:38)：想想，我们把我作为一种最终用户，经历整个旅程，假装我感兴趣，半感兴趣，我想从网站上购买。这样的事情吸引我吗？价值主张是否非常明确？然后从那里开始注册免费帐户或免费试用，顺利吗？当我开始使用该产品时，我是很快就恍然大悟，还是感到非常困惑和沮丧，在那一刻被抛弃了？从那时起，如果我觉得这很好，对吧，我顿悟了，我想买。我还可以买吗？你永远不会相信，就像我进行这次审计时一样，在这个过程中通常有这么多容易实现的目标。例如，一位客户，当我进入结账流程时，那种结账表格非常混乱。 (00:37:38)：他们问了一堆问题，我们只说英国客户的需求。其他地方他们不需要回答，但他们还是会问问题。作为一个美国人，我感到非常困惑，然后我就放弃了。还有其他事情，例如我所说的顿悟时刻。当我第一次接触产品时，我不知道该怎么做，我非常兴奋并准备好了，但我不知道该怎么做。我很失落和困惑。这通常是一个相当大的重点领域和机会领域。只是让您的用户顿悟时刻。他们已经克服了这里的许多障碍，但不要只是拒绝他们然后他们就离开，因为这太令人困惑了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: It might be helpful just to explain an aha moment. I know people hear this term a lot. What's a simple way to think about what is an aha moment?
turns.zh: 仅仅解释一下顿悟时刻可能会有所帮助。我知道人们经常听到这个词。思考什么是顿悟时刻的简单方法是什么？

turns.speaker: Hila Qu
turns.en: I think it as a moment, as a first time a user experienced value of your product. So it gets popular because Facebook has this example from the early growth days. I think you added 10 friends in seven days, you hit your aha moment. But there are many layers under that. The reason why Facebook used that to define its aha moment is because in early days, if you add these friends, you begin to form some connection. You can see an interesting feed, you can interact with your friends, and that social interaction, it's the core value of Facebook, and Facebook leaves by looking at a lot of data. If you meet that data metric criteria it's kind of very likely you will hit that aha moment. But I think for a lot of, especially we're talking about many SaaS product, B2B software, the value of such product is usually either you see a workflow can be supported by this, it can save your time, it can save your money, it can help you make more money, or it just solve this pain point that you never get to solve on your own without a software product. (00:39:57): So at GitLab we actually did a bunch of analysis. We're trying to understand what is the aha moment for our new users. We ended up have something along the line of two users, two features used in the first 14 days. So it's very similar to Facebook's kind of format. But deep down, because we are a platform, we are a team product, two users is talking about the team components. Whatever the first user is trying and using that is so valuable, he or she is confident to invite another coworker to come in. That itself is very, very valuable action and indicates this first user is seeing value. And if together they use two or more features, that means we are seeing the collaboration, the platform components of the product. And within the first 14 days, because it has to be reasonably quick but not unrealistic, because we are a complicated product, we're not Facebook, we're not Zynga or a game app, it's hard for you to figure it out in the first day. So yeah, I think it's a very important concept for any PLG company to figure out because that's often the biggest opportunity area I see.
turns.zh: 我认为这是一个时刻，作为用户第一次体验到你的产品的价值。所以它之所以受欢迎，是因为Facebook在早期成长时期就有这个例子。我认为您在 7 天内添加了 10 个朋友，您顿悟了。但其下还有很多层次。 Facebook 之所以用它来定义它的顿悟时刻，是因为在早期，如果你添加这些朋友，你就开始形成某种联系。你可以看到一个有趣的提要，你可以和你的朋友互动，而社交互动，这是Facebook的核心价值，而Facebook是通过查看大量数据而离开的。如果您满足该数据指标标准，那么您很可能会顿悟。但我认为对于很多，尤其是我们谈论的很多SaaS产品、B2B软件，这种产品的价值通常要么是你看到一个工作流程可以得到它的支持，它可以节省你的时间，它可以节省你的钱，它可以帮助你赚更多的钱，或者它只是解决这个没有软件产品你自己无法解决的痛点。 (00:39:57)：所以在 GitLab 我们实际上做了很多分析。我们试图了解新用户的顿悟时刻是什么。我们最终得到了两个用户在前 14 天内使用的一些东西。所以它与 Facebook 的格式非常相似。但内心深处，因为我们是一个平台，我们是一个团队产品，两个用户谈论的是团队组件。无论第一个用户正在尝试和使用什么，只要它非常有价值，他或她就有信心邀请其他同事加入。这本身就是非常非常有价值的行动，表明第一个用户正在看到价值。如果它们一起使用两个或多个功能，则意味着我们正在看到协作，即产品的平台组件。在前 14 天内，因为它必须相当快，但又不能不切实际，因为我们是一个复杂的产品，我们不是 Facebook，我们不是 Zynga 或游戏应用程序，所以你很难在第一天就弄清楚。所以，是的，我认为这对于任何 PLG 公司来说都是一个非常重要的概念，因为这通常是我看到的最大的机会领域。

turns.en: Yeah, exactly. So there are how you can get to that, right? First of all, the internal team, our growth team, actually we did some brainstorming. We think about what are the potential action or behavior that indicate they're getting value. We ideally want to do something like they maybe successfully merge their first PR or they successfully run their first pipeline. All of that. There are some potential high value actions we can think of. We just list all of them. And then the next step is, we did a correlation analysis to understand, hey, those are the 10 high value actions we believe we want to look at. If a new user did this action, what's the maybe 30 day conversion rate and... Not 30 day, 90 day conversion rate. What's the 30 day retention rate? Because we look at both. Sometimes you only look at retention or you only look at conversion, it doesn't give you the full picture. (00:42:52): So we look at if you did this action, let's say if, Lenny, you are trying our product, you are able to successfully merge the PR in your first 30 days. Does that improve your likelihood to convert? Does that improve your likelihood to retain? And we compare across those 10 high value actions, compare with the average. And we begin to see, oh, some actions actually if you do that, it lift your conversion, lift your retention much bigger. And those are the candidates for potential aha moments. And from there, the reason why we ended up not picking one single action... For some products, actually you can pick a single action. If one action really stands out, I don't know, for Airbnb [inaudible 00:43:39] is probably, you book a hotel, you go to there, you are so happy, you leave a high star review. That's the key action for this platform. (00:43:49): For GitLab, we have so many different workflow components. Teams are here for different reasons. Some are here for security, some are here for like CSAD. So that's why we ended up combining like two action. It can be any of the two high value features. The next step is actually you need to launch some experiments to try to get more people to do those high value action. And you then see, do I see higher conversion? Do I see higher retention? Because in data you are only isolating correlation. You are not proving causation. You just saw people who are doing this are more likely to convert. But it doesn't mean if you get people to do that, they will convert. So experimentation is the step. You will finally kind of validate that.

(00:56:48): Retention is super important, but it's a little bit messy. But how I think about retention, there are two steps. One is how to build a habit in their usage pattern, so that they are using this maybe every week, every day. The key to do that is, first of all, your product need to have a high enough frequency. If you are using this once per month, it's not likely you can build this into a habit. (00:57:39): Before GitLab, I worked at Acorns. We started as an investment app, and the whole thing is passive investment, passive investing. You bought some ETFs, and then you basically don't even need to check, and you just keep adding money and it will grow, and after 10 years is awesome. It's actually the right investment philosophy, but when I worked as a head of growth, it made a big challenge for me, because think about set and forget it. They don't even need to go back to a product to be successful. And that make it very hard, as a head of growth, to drive engagement, drive retention. I don't even know whether they're retained or not, if they are not coming back, right? I can only gauge from other indicators. So I think one thing I would say about building habit is think about how to build those habit feature or collaboration feature into your workflow already, into the product already. turns.zh: 是的，我知道我没有在帖子中谈论这一点，有人问，嘿，你打算再写一篇关于这个特定主题的帖子吗？因此，正如您所提到的，我没有讨论太多保留扩展的原因是，它通常不是第一个开始的地方。我把保留称为混乱的中间。它实际上是整个漏斗中混乱的一部分。快速激活、转换，这些都很快。有时这些时间跨度几乎较短，对吧？你有很多从未做过的事情，你可以很快地进行测试，而这种收购是一个非常大的杠杆。您始终需要获得更多用户。 (00:56:48)：保留非常重要，但有点混乱。这是一个很长的时间段，你的客户可以在任何特定的时刻，他们可以保留或不保留，就像如果他们只是取消或决定不再使用，你已经失去了他们，所以这是一个非常混乱的部分。但我如何看待保留，有两个步骤。一是如何在他们的使用模式中养成习惯，以便他们可能每周、每天都使用它。做到这一点的关键是，首先你的产品需要有足够高的频率。如果您每月使用一次，您不太可能将其养成习惯。 (00:57:39)：在 GitLab 之前，我在 Acorns 工作。我们一开始是一个投资应用程序，整个事情就是被动投资，被动投资。你买了一些ETF，然后你基本上甚至不需要检查，你只要不断加钱，它就会增长，10年后就很棒了。这实际上是正确的投资理念，但当我担任增长主管时，这对我来说是一个很大的挑战，因为想了想就忘记了。他们甚至不需要回到产品就能获得成功。这使得作为增长负责人很难提高参与度、提高保留率。我什至不知道他们是否被保留，如果他们不回来的话，对吗？我只能从其他指标来衡量。因此，我认为关于养成习惯我想说的一件事是考虑如何将这些习惯功能或协作功能构建到您的工作流程中，已经构建到产品中。从根本上来说，这就是他们能够保留的原因，如果它的频率很高，如果它涉及与其他人的协作，如果它是他们工作流程的一部分。这是第一步。显然你可以使用很多外观来强化这一点。如果他们采取某些行动，您可以向他们发送电子邮件，然后让他们回来，并重复该操作，但从根本上讲，您需要将其构建到您的产品中。 (00:59:09)：关于保留的下一部分是我实际上认为扩展是保留的一部分。基本上你已经有了稳定的使用流程。您每周、每天都会习惯性地使用它。什么时候最适合促使您考虑购买更多产品？以产品为主导的扩展分为三类。第一个是升级到更高级别。第二个是购买更多的种子，购买更多的许可证。第三个是如果你有某种消费附加组件，只是消费更多，对吧？就像GitLab一样，你可以从青铜级升级到白银级，你可以到更高的级别，然后你可以购买更多的种子，也可以购买更多的CSCD分钟来消耗。这些都是不同的时刻。要做到这一点，你需要真正理解数据、理解用法，并在正确的时间向正确的人触发大量正确的对话。 (01:00:17)：你可以再次强调，在激活转换中使用的许多类似策略实际上可以完美地应用在扩展中，因为这几乎是让人们对该功能产生恍然大悟、使用该功能、尝试该功能、让他们进行转换的组合。

We have some other very cool investment features called roundup investment, so nobody is really paying a lot of a attention on this, but when I look at data, I saw recurring investment has a high correlation with retention. So I did a lot of work trying to get more people to set this up, and which has been a great success, actually, in a very short period of time. (01:01:58): And then from there, I would say we begin to add more use cases that has a higher frequency, like I mentioned, right? If you only come here once per month to check our investment, it's very hard to retain you. We don't have any lever to engagement with you as well, if you are not in the product. turns.zh: 我认为有两件事。有一点其实和你刚才说的很相似。当我被要求从事保留工作时，我做了很多分析。对我来说最大的杠杆实际上是激活。所以我最终做了大量的激活实验。我确定了哪些功能可以让用户快速获取体验价值，从而更有可能保留。对我们来说，这是一个称为经常性投资的功能，事后看来这是有道理的，但当时没有人关心这一点。我们还有一些其他非常酷的投资功能，称为综合投资，所以没有人真正关注这一点，但当我查看数据时，我发现经常性投资与保留率具有很高的相关性。所以我做了很多工作试图让更多的人建立这个，实际上，在很短的时间内取得了巨大的成功。 (01:01:58)：然后从那里开始，我们开始添加更多频率更高的用例，就像我提到的，对吗？如果你每个月只来一次检查我们的投资，就很难留住你。如果您不在产品中，我们也没有任何手段与您互动。所以我们最终添加了 IRA 账户，即退休账户。我们最终添加了支出帐户，例如借记卡，例如更多的高频用例。这些用例本质上具有更高的频率和更好的保留率，因此现在您将问题从如何提高保留率转变为如何推动更高频率用例的采用？因此，我再次进行了一系列实验，如何推动更多人采用退休账户。一旦你有了退休账户（IRA），就会产生税务后果，所有这些。在那里你很难离开。因此，在这种情况下，您也可以将问题再次转化为采用/激活问题。

(01:06:12): The third piece I think that's pretty essential, I counted in the infra, is some sort of a lifecycle marketing tool. I know many B2B companies, they use HubSpot or they use something for their email marketing, but those are usually least nurturing. (01:07:10): And then from there, there are a lot of PLD tools you can add on top to make your day-to-day much easier. (01:07:52): For activation, a lot of my clients are finding a lot of value in those tools like Appcues, User-Led, basically the tools that allow you to build onboarding flow quickly in a product without engineer kind of resource. So you need to do some initial integration, but as soon as you did that a marketing manager, a PM or someone, can just build some customized onboarding step-by-step flows himself. I think that's quite neat, because you need to test the tongue in that area. (01:08:27): And in terms of conversion, I would say there are many product-led growth, product-led sales tools. I think those are great. If you want to build out your PQL/PQA conversion pass, think about Endgame, Pocus, Tableau and Pace. There are a couple of them.
turns.zh: 我说有两块。一个是基础设施，另一个是一些次要的工具。因此，从基础设施的角度来看，在数据工具上，我的第一个工具通常是某种数据中心部分，对吧？下一个是某种产品分析工具。考虑一下振幅。我知道 PostHog 实际上是一个非常受欢迎的。它是一个开源产品分析工具。有 Mixpanel、Pandle，所有这些。因此，要有某种数据中心、数据收集工具，并有某种产品分析工具。这就是数据基础设施。 (01:05:49)：然后你需要有一个实验工具，因为就像我说的，你不能想象你构建了所有东西并且一切都完美运行。所以你需要像 Optimizely 这样的东西，我知道 Amplitude 有一些实验组件。 Eppo 是一款即将推出的新产品。您需要一些工具来进行实验。 (01:06:12)：我认为非常重要的第三部分，我在下文中提到过，是某种生命周期营销工具。我知道很多 B2B 公司，他们使用 HubSpot 或者使用一些东西进行电子邮件营销，但这些通常是最不利于培养的。而且它与生命周期营销工具有很大不同，这意味着你需要连接Segment、Amplitude。您可以根据客户的行为，在正确的时间向正确的人了解客户正在使用您的产品、您的设计、您的电子邮件、您的应用内、您的推送通知。你衡量成功的标准是他们是否在产品中采取了正确的行动，而领先培育电子邮件营销工具是我让他们阅读文章，打开电子邮件，我为他们的领先分数添加 10 分，然后他们在列表漏斗中进一步前进？所以，数据工具、实验工具、生命周期营销工具，这些都是基础设施。 (01:07:10)：然后，您可以添加很多 PLD 工具，让您的日常工作变得更加轻松。首先，因为这对于获取来说是最重要的，您需要有某种类似数据丰富工具的工具。想想ZoomInfo、Clearbit，因为B2B和B2C最大的区别就是你还是需要了解他们的公司。你想了解这个人，但你也想了解这个人的公司，对吧？这是一件非常重要的事情，您可以从这些数据丰富工具中获得很多东西，然后您可以基于此以不同的方式设计您的旅程。 (01:07:52)：对于激活，我的很多客户都发现 Appcues、User-Led 等工具具有很大的价值，基本上这些工具可以让您在产品中快速构建入门流程，而无需工程师资源。因此，您需要进行一些初始集成，但一旦完成，营销经理、产品经理或其他人就可以自己构建一些定制的分步流程。我认为这非常巧妙，因为您需要测试该区域的舌头。 (01:08:27)：就转化而言，我想说有很多产品主导的增长、产品主导的销售工具。我认为这些都很棒。如果您想构建 PQL/PQA 转换过程，请考虑 Endgame、Pocus、Tableau 和 Pace。其中有几个。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Wow. Amazing. That was an awesome list and really well-structured. Is there anything else along the data or infrastructure piece that you want to touch on before we move on to hiring and the team?
turns.zh: 哇。惊人的。这是一个很棒的清单，而且结构非常好。在我们继续招聘和团队之前，您还想谈一下数据或基础设施方面的其他内容吗？

turns.speaker: Hila Qu
turns.en: I just want to go back to the point, as I mentioned, product-led growth is data-led growth deep down. So in most of the situation when I see a company want to get started, where they are really missing or they need to invest more, is data. So if you identify you have a gap in this area, don't feel bad as well. A lot of pretty big companies are in the same shoes, and if you can't invest the time, money, the team, the tool, to figure this out, the benefit of this, right, the data collection, understanding usage data, can not only power your PLG motion, it can really power your entire product team, even your customer success team. Now you gave them the ingredients they need to develop the next feature, based on not only what your top customer asked for, but also what everybody's using, right? (01:09:59): Your customer success team can take a much deeper view in understanding what the clients are using, rather than just talk with the executives from the client and get a rough gauge of the situation. So I think it is a area worth investing, and every B2B company should be investing in.
turns.zh: 我只想回到这一点，正如我提到的，产品主导的增长本质上是数据主导的增长。因此，在大多数情况下，当我看到一家公司想要起步时，他们确实缺少或需要投入更多，那就是数据。因此，如果您发现自己在这方面存在差距，也不要感到难过。很多相当大的公司都处于同样的境地，如果你不能投入时间、金钱、团队、工具来解决这个问题，那么数据收集、理解使用数据的好处不仅可以推动你的 PLG 行动，它还可以真正推动你的整个产品团队，甚至你的客户成功团队。现在，您为他们提供了开发下一个功能所需的成分，不仅基于您的顶级客户的要求，还基于每个人都在使用的内容，对吗？ (01:09:59)：您的客户成功团队可以更深入地了解客户正在使用的产品，而不仅仅是与客户的高管交谈并粗略地了解情况。所以我认为这是一个值得投资的领域，每个B2B公司都应该投资。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I'm trying to channel what listeners might be thinking right now, and I imagine some people might be like what if I pick the wrong tool? I'm kind of stressed, I have to do all this research. I'm kind of worried about starting, because it'll set me up for failure later. Which of these buckets do you think is most important to get right, right from the beginning, and any advice on how to just avoid messing that up?
turns.zh: 我正在尝试传达听众现在的想法，我想有些人可能会想，如果我选择了错误的工具怎么办？我有点压力，我必须做所有这些研究。我对开始有点担心，因为这会让我以后失败。您认为从一开始就正确处理这些问题中的哪一个是最重要的？关于如何避免搞砸这一点有什么建议吗？

turns.speaker: Hila Qu
turns.en: To get started, I would say probably a product analytics tool is the first step, and maybe the data hub, such as Segment. So if you have Segment and particle tools like that, it allows you to plug into so many different tools. You can basically try all the different tools, and if it doesn't work, you just flip a switch, you can try another tool. So there is a benefit there, but it is expensive, so I know companies may just go right into the product analytics tool. I would say it's hard to get it wrong completely, right? (01:11:19): In order for a product analytics tool to be meaningful, the first step is you need to collect the data, you need to do some instrumentation, you need to have the foundation. And then, because it's garbage in, garbage out, if you send a bunch of garbage data into your product analytics tool, your analyst will be just even more confusing, right? It's like he doesn't know whether to trust the data, what to use. So a lot of company I work with, the first step is maybe not looking into tool, but do an audit of your data instrumentation situation, to understand how many of the key actions are intact, is the format correct, is the data, what are the gaps? And you may need to do some re-instrumenta ...
turns.zh: 首先，我想说产品分析工具可能是第一步，也许还有数据中心，例如 Segment。因此，如果您有这样的分段和粒子工具，它就可以让您插入许多不同的工具。你基本上可以尝试所有不同的工具，如果它不起作用，你只需翻转一个开关，你就可以尝试另一个工具。所以这是有好处的，但它很昂贵，所以我知道公司可能会直接使用产品分析工具。我想说很难完全弄错，对吧？ (01:11:19)：为了使产品分析工具有意义，第一步是您需要收集数据，您需要进行一些检测，您需要具备基础。然后，因为它是垃圾输入，垃圾输出，如果你将一堆垃圾数据发送到你的产品分析工具中，你的分析师会更加困惑，对吧？就好像他不知道是否应该相信这些数据，该使用什么。因此，与我合作的很多公司，第一步可能不是研究工具，而是对您的数据仪器情况进行审核，以了解有多少关键操作是完整的，格式是否正确，数据是否正确，有哪些差距？而且您可能需要进行一些重新检测...

turns.speaker: Hila Qu
turns.en: Right, what are the gaps? And you may need to do some reinstrumentation, reformatting and things like that before you even plug into a product analytics to make it useful.
turns.zh: 对了，还有哪些差距呢？在插入产品分析以使其发挥作用之前，您可能需要进行一些重新检测、重新格式化等操作。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: For someone that may want to do that audit, is there a thing you would point them to, or, I don't know, a blog, a course, something to help them understand if they're doing it right? Or is it like, "Bring Hila on," and you need someone like you to kind of help them through it?
turns.zh: 对于可能想要进行审核的人，您是否可以向他们指出一些东西，或者，我不知道，一个博客，一个课程，一些东西可以帮助他们了解他们是否做得正确？或者就像是“带上海拉”，你需要像你这样的人来帮助他们度过难关？

turns.speaker: Hila Qu
turns.en: No, you can bring me, but you don't have to bring me. I think there are, if you search on Google just the data dictionary, or data product usage, data audit, a lot of companies published template and spreadsheet you can use. I can even send you a few afterwards.
turns.zh: 不，你可以带我，但你不必带我。我认为，如果你在谷歌上搜索数据字典，或者数据产品使用情况、数据审计、很多公司发布的模板和电子表格，你可以使用。之后我什至可以给你发一些。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That'd be amazing.
turns.zh: 那真是太棒了。

turns.speaker: Hila Qu
turns.en: And then you can just scroll through. Basically the key idea is go through your product experience, identify the key actions, and go through your data instrumentation and see, "Do they match?" (01:12:57): And the success of this is you identify the gaps and eventually you want to establish something called the data dictionary. I basically do that for a lot of my clients. And the data dictionary will include, here are all the key actions, what's the event name for each of those, and what are the property and things like that. (01:13:17): But you now know, "Hey, I have this action track, this is the name. If I have a new product manager or analyst, we can all refer to this." And everyone know the same definition rather than people are interpreting differently. So that's a very important part to success even before the tooling.
turns.zh: 然后你就可以滚动浏览。基本上，关键思想是回顾您的产品体验，确定关键操作，然后查看您的数据工具并查看“它们匹配吗？” (01:12:57)：成功的关键在于你找出了差距，最终你想要建立一种称为数据字典的东西。我基本上为很多客户这样做。数据字典将包括所有关键操作、每个操作的事件名称以及属性和类似内容。 (01:13:17)：但是你现在知道了，“嘿，我有这个行动轨迹，这就是名字。如果我有新的产品经理或分析师，我们都可以参考这个。”每个人都知道相同的定义，而不是人们的解释不同。因此，即使在使用工具之前，这也是成功的一个非常重要的部分。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Awesome. It also reminds me a previous guest, Crystal Widjaja, has a awesome post on why most analytics efforts fail. And she talks a lot about this, of how to set your events up for success. So we'll link to that as well.
turns.zh: 惊人的。这也让我想起了之前的一位嘉宾 Crystal Widjaja，她发表了一篇精彩的文章，阐述了大多数分析工作失败的原因。她谈到了很多关于如何让你的活动取得成功的话题。所以我们也会链接到它。

turns.speaker: Hila Qu
turns.en: Mm-hm.
turns.zh: 嗯嗯。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Maybe one last thing here, I'm trying to think about what would screw people up most, and it's probably not having a data warehouse and ETL sorts of tooling in place, because that feeds a lot of this.
turns.zh: 也许这里的最后一件事是，我试图思考什么会让人们最烦恼，而且可能没有适当的数据仓库和 ETL 类型的工具，因为这提供了很多东西。

turns.speaker: Hila Qu
turns.en: Yep.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Is there anything you want to add there about just the importance of a data warehouse and how to set that up?
turns.zh: 关于数据仓库的重要性以及如何设置它，您有什么想要补充的吗？

turns.speaker: Hila Qu
turns.en: Some of the early stage companies I work with, when they just get started in the very beginning, they don't have data warehouse. They just basically have their product and they have some sort of a Google Analytics or Amplitude, and that's it. It's pretty wild, but it's working and they can get to someplace from there. (01:14:25): But as soon as you begin to have data user, it's time to get serious to establish a data warehouse, have some ETL solution. I think there are the most common best practice ones, like AWS and things like that. There are also some startups that are doing this and you can utilize as well. (01:14:49): But again, as soon as you become a serious business, you should invest in that. Otherwise, it's pretty wild and it's pretty fragile as well.
turns.zh: 我合作过的一些早期公司，当他们刚刚起步时，他们没有数据仓库。他们基本上只是拥有自己的产品，并且拥有某种 Google Analytics 或 Amplitude，仅此而已。这很疯狂，但是很有效，他们可以从那里到达某个地方。 (01:14:25): 但是一旦你开始拥有数据用户，就该认真建立一个数据仓库，拥有一些 ETL 解决方案。我认为有最常见的最佳实践，例如 AWS 之类的。还有一些初创公司正在这样做，您也可以利用。 (01:14:49)：但是，一旦你成为一家严肃的企业，你就应该对此进行投资。否则，它非常狂野，也非常脆弱。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And when you say AWS, you mean at Redshift, I imagine?
turns.zh: 我想，当您说 AWS 时，您指的是 Redshift？

turns.speaker: Hila Qu
turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Cool. Awesome. Okay, final area that we have time for, which is awesome, which is around building your team. So maybe just two questions here. What is your advice for starting the initial team investing in PLG? How does that usually look and what do you think people should do? And then later, how does that evolve over time?
turns.zh: 凉爽的。惊人的。好的，我们还有时间讨论的最后一个领域，这很棒，那就是建立你的团队。所以也许这里只有两个问题。对于启动投资 PLG 的初始团队，您有何建议？通常情况下，您认为人们应该做什么？然后，随着时间的推移，这种情况会如何演变？

turns.speaker: Hila Qu
turns.en: How I see most companies started is the founder or the leadership team realize that they need to do PLG. And they build a conviction. Maybe initially there isn't even a dedicated team, but they did something here and there, they decided to invest in this. (01:15:40): And the common place to start is to hire a head of growth, or it can be a lead growth PM, but someone who has a little bit of experience in this area. And then they begin to build this core growth squad as the first growth team. And I think that's a very common place to start. (01:16:01): The other place to start that's less common, but I also think it happening in reality, is maybe they will start a cross-functional, almost like a tiger team. Because if the initial focus area is, let's say, they want to do a product qualified lead, or basically add that funnel. That involves not only product team, that will involve data team because you want to know what are the usage pattern that indicate these is better leads. You also need to bring sales team in because they need to work on those leads to close them. (01:16:39): So if that's the initial starting area, a cross-functional tiger team is also possible option. But the most common way is hire a head of growth, usually a growth PM, and then start a team with engineering, design, data to support that core growth squad.
turns.zh: 我认为大多数公司的起步方式是创始人或领导团队意识到他们需要进行 PLG。他们建立了信念。也许最初甚至没有专门的团队，但他们到处做了一些事情，他们决定对此进行投资。 (01:15:40)：通常的起点是聘请增长主管，或者可以是首席增长 PM，但要在该领域有一点经验。然后他们开始打造这个核心成长团队，作为第一成长团队。我认为这是一个非常常见的起点。 (01:16:01)：另一个不太常见的起点，但我也认为现实中会发生这种情况，也许他们会组建一个跨职能的团队，就像老虎团队一样。因为如果最初的重点领域是，比如说，他们想要做一个合格的产品领导者，或者基本上添加那个漏斗。这不仅涉及产品团队，还涉及数据团队，因为您想知道表明这些是更好的潜在客户的使用模式是什么。您还需要让销售团队参与，因为他们需要处理这些潜在客户以关闭它们。 (01:16:39)：因此，如果这是最初的起始区域，那么跨职能的老虎团队也是可能的选择。但最常见的方法是聘请一名增长主管，通常是增长 PM，然后组建一个工程、设计、数据团队来支持核心增长团队。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And the main difference between these two. One is dedicated, "We are going to dedicate full-time people to helping us grow." Like I say we talked about earlier, let's say they're going to focus on activation and that's their whole job. Versus tiger team is basically they're borrowing resources from other teams and this is kind of a side project for them.
turns.zh: 以及这两者之间的主要区别。一是专注，“我们将投入全职人员来帮助我们成长。”就像我说的，我们之前谈到过，假设他们将专注于激活，这就是他们的全部工作。与 Tiger 团队相比，他们基本上是从其他团队借用资源，这对他们来说是一个副项目。

turns.speaker: Hila Qu
turns.en: Yeah. A little bit, for a period of time. So it's temporary. It's kind of they almost to want to get into... I would say usually the cross-functional team, the tiger team, is a little bit prior to a full commitment. They're pretty much committed, but they still want to try this out and get a final conviction, and then they begin to dedicate resources. (01:17:43): And you ask about how do they evolve from there.
turns.zh: 是的。一点点，一段时间。所以这是暂时的。他们几乎想要进入……我想说的是，通常跨职能团队，即老虎团队，在做出全面承诺之前会稍早一些。他们非常坚定，但他们仍然想尝试一下并得到最终的信念，然后他们开始投入资源。 (01:17:43)：你问他们是如何从那里演变而来的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Before we actually get there, maybe one more quick question. Which would you recommend? I imagine you'd recommend a dedicated team, if you can do that.
turns.zh: 在我们真正到达那里之前，也许还有一个简单的问题。您会推荐哪一个？我想如果你能做到的话，你会推荐一个专门的团队。

turns.speaker: Hila Qu
turns.en: Mm-hm.
turns.zh: 嗯嗯。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: When would it make sense to go the tiger team route? In what cases?
turns.zh: 什么时候走老虎队路线才有意义？什么情况下？

turns.speaker: Hila Qu
turns.en: One situation I would recommend is that if the initial focus area is, like I said, product qualified leads, the sales conversion path. Because if you think about you have a head of growth or a core growth PM, that person usually has a growth PM background and is in the product organization. And they're awesome if the initial focus areas are activation, conversion, those kind of involve a lot of experimentation. But activation and conversion are relatively confined, it's something the growth PM and engineer design data, they can work on. (01:18:39): If your initial focus area you felt like, "My biggest bit is actually do this PQL thing," it is a little bit harder for the growth PM to socialize all those cross-functional resources, because he need to get pretty deep into data. He need to have a counterpart in sales, even in marketing. So in that case, I think it's possible that maybe you start a tiger team. (01:19:03): You can combine both. You can have a growth PM dedicated, but have some tiger team to be working with him or her on this PQL project as well.
turns.zh: 我建议的一种情况是，如果最初的重点领域是，就像我说的，产品合格的潜在客户，销售转化路径。因为如果您认为自己有一位增长主管或核心增长 PM，那么该人通常具有增长 PM 背景并且在产品组织中。如果最初的重点领域是激活、转化，那么它们就很棒，这些涉及大量的实验。但激活和转换相对有限，这是增长 PM 和工程师设计数据可以处理的事情。 (01:18:39)：如果您最初关注的领域是“我最重要的事情实际上是做 PQL 事情”，那么增长 PM 社交化所有这些跨职能资源会有点困难，因为他需要深入了解数据。他需要在销售方面有一个对手，甚至在营销方面也是如此。所以在这种情况下，我认为你可能会组建一支老虎队。 (01:19:03)：您可以将两者结合起来。您可以有一位专门的增长 PM，但也可以有一些老虎团队与他或她在这个 PQL 项目上合作。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Got it. And I like this term tiger team, by the way. I haven't heard that before. It sounds like a lot of fun. Very dynamic. Okay, cool. And then yeah, what happens next after you have this initial team?
turns.zh: 知道了。顺便说一句，我喜欢老虎队这个词。我以前没听说过。听起来很有趣。非常有活力。好吧，酷。是的，在你拥有这个最初的团队之后接下来会发生什么？

turns.speaker: Hila Qu
turns.en: Once you have this initial team, it's important to give them the resources they need, and give them an initial focus area, give them support and a little bit time, allow them to try things out and get some early wins. And early win is the biggest thing I would say for, and whenever you start a new growth team, try to look for some opportunity, try to get some early wins in whichever focus area you choose. (01:19:53): And from there, if you get some of the wins, the team has some momentum, there are more confidence from the organization in PLG, right? It's time to potentially extend and formalize. So fundamentally I think you should not only think about the PLG team, you should think about the PLG org. Because PLG is a motion, it's cross-functional by nature, it's not just a product team or growth team. (01:20:24): Eventually you need to get to the place basically there is a head of growth product, that's the center of the PLG org. But there's also need to be a head of growth marketing, that's his or her counterpart in marketing organization. And then a head of product led sales, that's the counterpart in the sales organization. (01:20:47): Exactly where they sit, how they sit, it's different company by company. The most common one is head of growth product report to product org, head of growth marketing report to marketing, head of product led sales report to sales. But they have some sort of a very strong collaboration, because they are working in the same motion and same funnel. But I think that's next step, think about this org. (01:21:11): Once you have those counterparts in product, in sales, in marketing, the next step is think about what are the metrics they own to make sure you can manage this funnel, this motion, in the data-driven way. Because the PLG metrics are very different from SLG. The top of funnel is more about high quality signups. You don't want a lot of traffic, you want free signup, free trials. But it need to meet certain quality bar, it's not just anyone. (01:21:46): And then the head of growth product, he or her top KPI is about usage, activation. Activated teams is a very common metric. And then maybe number of PQLs, that's another. You want to get those teams to certain usage threshold basically. (01:22:07): And then the head of product led sales, he will be focused on converting those PQLs into revenue. So he will focus a lot on conversion rate, efficiency and maybe revenue, things like that.
turns.zh: 一旦你拥有了这个初始团队，重要的是为他们提供所需的资源，并为他们提供最初的重点领域，为他们提供支持和一点时间，让他们尝试新事物并获得一些早期胜利。早期的胜利是我想说的最重要的事情，每当你组建一个新的增长团队时，尝试寻找一些机会，尝试在你选择的重点领域获得一些早期的胜利。 (01:19:53)：从那里开始，如果你取得了一些胜利，球队就会有一些动力，组织对 PLG 就会更有信心，对吗？是时候进行潜在的扩展和正式化了。所以从根本上来说，我认为你不应该只考虑 PLG 团队，你应该考虑 PLG 组织。因为 PLG 是一项运动，所以它本质上是跨职能的，它不仅仅是一个产品团队或增长团队。 (01:20:24)：最终你需要到达一个地方，基本上有一个增长产品的负责人，这是 PLG 组织的中心。但还需要有一名增长营销主管，这是他或她在营销组织中的对应人员。然后由产品主管领导销售，这是销售组织中的对应人员。 (01:20:47)：具体他们坐的位置、坐的方式，每个公司都不同。最常见的一种是增长产品负责人向产品组织报告，增长营销负责人向营销人员报告，产品负责人向销售人员领导销售报告。但他们有某种非常强有力的合作，因为他们以相同的动作和相同的渠道工作。但我认为这是下一步，想想这个组织。 (01:21:11)：一旦你在产品、销售、营销方面有了这些同行，下一步就是考虑他们拥有哪些指标，以确保你可以以数据驱动的方式管理这个渠道、这个动作。因为PLG指标和SLG有很大不同。漏斗的顶部更多的是关于高质量的注册。您不需要大量流量，您想要免费注册、免费试用。但它需要满足一定的质量标准，而不是任何人。 (01:21:46)：然后是增长产品的负责人，他或她的首要 KPI 是关于使用、激活。活跃团队是一个非常常见的指标。然后也许是 PQL 的数量，这是另一个问题。基本上，您想让这些团队达到一定的使用阈值。 (01:22:07)：然后由产品负责人领导销售，他将专注于将这些 PQL 转化为收入。所以他会非常关注转化率、效率，也许还有收入，诸如此类的事情。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Got it. And you're sharing a lot of org design verbally in the post, which we'll share obviously in the show notes. You can actually see a diagram of what these look like, to help kind of make it super clear. (01:22:36): I have maybe just one more question. Going back to the initial team, what are the functions you recommend they have on this like MVP PLG team?
turns.zh: 知道了。您在帖子中口头分享了很多组织设计，我们将在演出笔记中明确分享。您实际上可以看到这些外观的图表，以帮助使其变得非常清晰。 (01:22:36)：我可能还有一个问题。回到最初的团队，您建议他们在像 MVP PLG 团队这样的团队中具有哪些功能？

turns.speaker: Hila Qu
turns.en: The most important one is have a growth PM to be the lead, right? Head of growth, director of growth, lead growth PM. And then the growth PM, as you know probably very well, growth PM, he is a PM but has a much stronger skill set in analytics, experimentation, very data-driven. Think about metrics. (01:23:06): The growth PM's way of working is similar to other product manager, but his KPIs is actually more similar to the sales and marketing work. He's very focused on the conversion rate, the journey, the funnel versus the feature specifically itself. (01:23:23): And then the other functions you need to have for sure, I would often say actually a data analyst needs to be the very first hire. Sometimes even try to find a growth PM who can do analysis if you're really small, you can find that type of unicorn person. (01:23:43): Or even before hiring growth PM, hiring analyst, I would actually go as far as that. Because without insight, without a lot of foundation, your experimentation, your effort is really directionless in a sense. (01:23:58): So growth PM, analyst. And from there definitely you need some dedicated engineer, you need a designer. Designer can be somewhat not dedicated in early days, but engineer needs to be. Some sort of user research support as well, it doesn't need to be dedicated. But those are the core growth squad.
turns.zh: 最重要的是有一位增长 PM 来领导，对吧？增长主管、增长总监、首席增长 PM。然后是增长 PM，正如您可能非常了解的那样，增长 PM，他是一名 PM，但在分析、实验、非常数据驱动方面拥有更强的技能。考虑指标。 (01:23:06): 增长PM的工作方式与其他产品经理类似，但他的KPI实际上更类似于销售和营销工作。他非常关注转化率、旅程、渠道与功能本身。 (01:23:23)：然后你肯定需要具备其他功能，我经常说实际上数据分析师需要成为第一个雇员。有时甚至尝试找一个可以做分析的增长PM，如果你很小的话，你可以找到那种类型的独角兽人。 (01:23:43)：或者甚至在聘请增长经理、招聘分析师之前，我实际上会这么做。因为如果没有洞察力，没有很多基础，你的实验、你的努力在某种意义上就真的是没有方向的。 (01:23:58)：所以增长PM，分析师。从那里你肯定需要一些专门的工程师，你需要一个设计师。设计师在早期可能有些不敬业，但工程师需要如此。还有某种用户研究支持，不需要专门提供。但这些都是核心成长阵容。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay. Real actual last question here for the growth PM. In your experience, are they most often coming from within the company already and they kind of shift to this role? Or do you recommend they find someone externally?
turns.zh: 好的。真正实际的最后一个问题是针对增长 PM 的。根据您的经验，他们是否通常已经来自公司内部，并且已经转变为这个角色？或者您建议他们找外部人员？

turns.speaker: Hila Qu
turns.en: That's an excellent question. I have seen both. I actually recommend if you can find someone internally, maybe he's a PM, he want to do growth. Or he is an analyst who want to become more like a product role. (01:24:48): I even have a one client, the head of growth I work with used to be a investor relationship, like head of investor relationship. And he reports to the CEO and founder. He's very analytical. He hasn't been a PM before, but he can socialize the resource within the company to launch experiments in product, in marketing, in all of that. And I, as an advisor, will come in, guide him in the area he's not familiar with. And we actually drive pretty good results together. (01:25:20): So I think prefer hiring internally if possible. If not, if you really don't have anyone internally with that knowledge or with that interest, you can look outside. I would say map the initial growth PM hire to your starting point. If we already decided activation is the biggest focus area, try to find some growth PM with that experience. And if the conversion is a focus area, acquisition is the focus area, try to find someone with that experience.
turns.zh: 这是一个很好的问题。我都见过。我实际上建议如果你能在内部找到一个人，也许他是一名产品经理，他想做增长。或者他是一名分析师，希望变得更像一个产品角色。 (01:24:48)：我什至有一个客户，与我合作的增长主管曾经是投资者关系主管，就像投资者关系主管一样。他向首席执行官和创始人汇报。他非常善于分析。他以前没有担任过产品经理，但他可以将公司内部的资源社交化，在产品、营销等所有方面开展实验。我作为顾问，会介入，在他不熟悉的领域指导他。事实上，我们共同取得了很好的成果。 (01:25:20)：所以我认为如果可能的话更喜欢内部招聘。如果没有，如果你内部确实没有人具备这种知识或兴趣，你可以向外寻找。我想说的是，将初始增长的 PM 聘用映射到你的起点。如果我们已经确定激活是最大的重点领域，请尝试寻找一些具有该经验的增长产品经理。如果转换是重点领域，获取是重点领域，请尝试找到具有这种经验的人。

turns.speaker: Hila Qu
turns.en: This first one is called The Almanack Of Naval. Yeah, I don't know whether we read that one. I really love that one. That's kind of a life-changing book for me. I have it-
turns.zh: 第一个叫做《海军年鉴》。是的，我不知道我们是否读过那一篇。我真的很喜欢那个。这对我来说是一本改变生活的书。我有它-

turns.en: Do you have a favorite Naval-ism that comes to mind?

I gifted this to a lot of my female team member and I really learned a lot from them. (01:26:56): And the third one is my book, it's called [Chinese 01:27:01]. It's only in Chinese, if you don't read Chinese you cannot read it. But I heard, my friends told me, if you are launching an email campaign, if you're doing experiments, have this book by the side, it will help with conversion rate just by its appearance.
turns.zh: 我从他那里学会了寻找杠杆。他谈到杠杆有四种类型。可以是你的文字，可以是代码，可以是资本，可以是团队。所以我在写作上投入大量资金的原因是我觉得这就是我的杠杆。我喜欢这样。 (01:26:44)：第二本书名为《女性如何崛起》。我真的很喜欢这个。我把这个礼物送给了我的很多女性团队成员，我真的从她们身上学到了很多东西。 (01:26:56)：第三本是我的书，叫做[中文01:27:01]。只有中文，如果你不读中文，你就看不懂。但我听说，我的朋友告诉我，如果你正在发起电子邮件营销活动，如果你正在做实验，请把这本书放在身边，光是它的外观就会有助于提高转化率。

turns.en: It's only in Chinese, so you have to learn.
turns.zh: 只有中文，所以你必须学习。

turns.zh: 好吧，我明白了。好的。这是一个优势，如果你会说中文，你的电子邮件转化率就会上升。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Favorite interview question that you like to ask.
turns.zh: 您最喜欢问的面试问题。

turns.speaker: Hila Qu
turns.en: When I interview a growth PM or analyst, I will always ask, "What is a experiment you launched that has a very unexpected result? And what did you do after that?"
turns.zh: 当我采访增长型产品经理或分析师时，我总是会问：“你发起的一项实验有什么结果却产生了非常意想不到的结果？之后你做了什么？”

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: What do you look for in an answer there that makes you feel like they are strong?
turns.zh: 你在答案中寻找什么让你觉得他们很坚强？

turns.speaker: Hila Qu
turns.en: So first of all, they have to be launching a lot of experiments to get very unexpected answer. So if you are only... Many people remember their success for the interview, they prepare that very well. I don't want to ask, "What's your successful experiment?" (01:28:58): Secondly, I want to know just why it's unexpected. That reveals the deep, deep level of their thinking, how deep they are thinking. If they should expect that based on what they described, then they are not thinking deep enough, they are not understanding customer enough. (01:29:15): And what they do afterwards is also awesome. Like, "How do you face a failure or unexpected result? What are the clues you can pursue? What are the actions you can take? How do you learn something out of it?"
turns.zh: 所以首先，他们必须进行大量的实验才能得到非常意想不到的答案。所以，如果你只是……很多人都记得他们面试的成功，他们准备得很好。我不想问“你成功的实验是什么？” (01:28:58)：其次，我想知道为什么会出乎意料。这揭示了他们的思考的深层次，他们的思考有多深。如果他们应该根据他们的描述来预期这一点，那么他们的思考不够深入，他们对客户的理解不够。 (01:29:15)：他们之后所做的事情也很棒。比如，“你如何面对失败或意想不到的结果？你可以追寻哪些线索？你可以采取哪些行动？你如何从中学到一些东西？”

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I love it. What's a favorite recent product you've recently discovered that you love?
turns.zh: 我喜欢它。您最近发现的最喜欢的产品是什么？

turns.speaker: Hila Qu
turns.en: I would say, similar to everyone, ChatGPT. But also Lululemon yoga pants.
turns.zh: 我想说，和大家一样，ChatGPT。还有 Lululemon 瑜伽裤。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Amazing. Great. What's something relatively minor you've changed in your product development process that has had a tremendous impact on a team's ability to execute?
turns.zh: 惊人的。伟大的。您在产品开发过程中进行了哪些相对较小的更改，但对团队的执行能力产生了巨大影响？

turns.speaker: Hila Qu
turns.en: Yeah. At first I added basically a section in the dock, in the ticket stack. Ask the PMs to write the success metric ahead of time. As well as adding which of the growth lever this is helping. Is this contributing to acquisition, activation, retention, monetization? And it forced them to sometimes think through deeply, "Why are we even doing this?" Sometimes they ended up not doing that by just writing it down.
turns.zh: 是的。起初，我基本上在码头的票务堆栈中添加了一个部分。要求产品经理提前写出成功指标。以及增加增长杠杆这有帮助。这是否有助于获取、激活、保留、货币化？这迫使他们有时深入思考，“我们为什么要这样做？”有时他们只是把它写下来，最终却没有做到这一点。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I love that. Next question. I know you're big on children's books, do you have a favorite children's book?
turns.zh: 我喜欢那个。下一个问题。我知道你很喜欢儿童读物，你有最喜欢的儿童读物吗？

turns.speaker: Hila Qu
turns.en: My favorite children's book is called Someday, and I recommend everyone to check it out. And basically it's talking about how our children used to be our baby, become our kids, and when they are taller and more stronger than us and they will remember us.
turns.zh: 我最喜欢的儿童读物是《有一天》，我推荐大家都看一下。基本上，它谈论的是我们的孩子如何曾经是我们的婴儿，成为我们的孩子，当他们比我们更高、更强壮时，他们会记住我们。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I'm going to need to check that out now. And final question. I know you're big on growth concepts, you have all these frameworks and concepts. And so what is your favorite growth concept?
turns.zh: 我现在需要检查一下。最后一个问题。我知道您热衷于增长概念，您拥有所有这些框架和概念。那么您最喜欢的增长理念是什么？

turns.speaker: Hila Qu
turns.en: I would say north star metric, because I find it's not only valuable to growth, it's valuable to just everything. (01:31:10): When I think about what do I want to do with my career, does that fit my own personal north star metric? When I think about how I want to raise my kids, I think about what's the north star metric for successful education for my kid? (01:31:27): Because it forced me to think long term. It forced me to think about what's valuable to me, to them, not only by the society standards, ARR revenue, like salary. And also what's my vision for myself and for my kids.
turns.zh: 我会说北极星指标，因为我发现它不仅对增长有价值，而且对一切都有价值。 (01:31:10)：当我思考我想在职业生涯中做什么时，这符合我个人的北极星指标吗？当我思考我想如何抚养我的孩子时，我会想我的孩子成功教育的北极星指标是什么？ (01:31:27)：因为它迫使我进行长远思考。它迫使我思考什么对我、对他们有价值，而不仅仅是社会标准、ARR 收入，比如工资。还有我对自己和孩子的愿景是什么。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I love that. It reminds me of a recent guest where she always asks, "What are you optimizing for?" Whether she's talking with her kids or her husband or her team, and it's a similar concept. (01:31:54): Hila, this was incredible. I think we've shared tens of thousands of dollars of value, and it will probably lead to millions of dollars of revenue for a lot of companies. And it's everything I hoped it would be.
